label: Jay Stratton
narrative: Stratton is the pivot between the legacy effort and the official one. He is publicly identified as the director of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force during its operative period, 2020-2021, the body Deputy Secretary of Defense David Norquist approved on 4 August 2020 and placed under the Department of the Navy with Office of Naval Intelligence cognizance. It was Stratton's task force that produced the classified underpinnings of the ODNI Preliminary Assessment delivered to Congress on 25 June 2021 - the report that put 144 incidents on the public record and conceded that 143 of them could not be explained. Grusch's account places the same office at the centre of the containment problem: he testified that in 2019 the UAP Task Force Director tasked him to identify every special access programme relevant to the Task Force's congressionally mandated mission, and that the read-ons were then refused. Stratton's earlier career runs through the DIA and the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program orbit, and he has spoken publicly about a personal sighting and about the Task Force's findings. He retired from government at the end of 2021, before AARO existed, and in September 2024 HarperCollins imprint William Morrow acquired rights to his memoir - an announcement that is itself a documented fact about the trajectory of a man who once ran the government's UAP portfolio. AARO absorbed his Task Force by direction of the 15 July 2022 establishment memorandum, which ordered the Secretary of the Navy to disestablish the UAPTF and transfer its data and materials.
